markers.title: Clocking in without the queue
markers.finding: The journey opens with three people waiting at the time clock at changeover. A fifteen year old arrives fifteen minutes early and still clocks in late, and his manager starts her shift approving late clock-ins that nobody caused. The report names the gap as no queuing system or second clock-in point, and no allowance for arrival time.
markers.decision: Clocking in from a phone, inside the restaurant only, inside a fifteen minute window either side of the rostered start. The terminal stays for anyone without a phone or without the policy to use one.
markers.rejected: A second terminal, which measures the queue rather than removing it and costs hardware in 900 restaurants.

markers.title: The break you are on, as a clock
markers.finding: Team members said they wanted to see how much time was left on a break, and were coming back saying they had another five minutes. There were no notifications for when a break should end.
markers.decision: A ring and a countdown, with a nudge at five minutes that goes to the person and the manager at the same time.
markers.rejected: A start and end time in a list, which is what the shift detail showed and which nobody can do arithmetic on mid-shift.

markers.title: Your own punch times
markers.finding: Punch times were not visible in the app and there was no clock in or out history, so verifying a time meant asking a manager. One interview recorded that being an issue from the beginning.
markers.decision: Every punch for the period, with the break inside it, and an amended punch shown as an amendment with who added it and why.
markers.rejected: Showing only the corrected figure, which quietly replaces what the clock recorded and gives a person nothing to query.

markers.title: A leave balance that is true today
markers.finding: Balances only moved at the pay run. Managers approved leave people had not accrued, and payroll absorbed the enquiries.
markers.decision: The balance updates after each shift is clocked out of, and expected pay updates with it, which were the two figures people asked for most.
markers.rejected: A balance as at the last pay run, which is accurate on one day a fortnight.

markers.title: A day of leave is a day on the list
markers.finding: Approved leave did not appear on the shift list, so a day off looked the same as a gap and people rang the restaurant to check the leave had gone through.
markers.decision: Leave sits in the list as a day, in its own colour, with the hours it draws and when the person agreed to it.
markers.rejected: A separate leave screen, which means checking two places to answer one question.
